items: India's debt-to-GDP ratio for FY26 stood at 58.2%, 210 bps higher than the 56.1% target, while fiscal deficit declined to 4.4%.
**Debt-to-GDP Ratio:** Government debt-to-GDP ratio for FY26 stood at **58.2%**.
**Target Deviation:** Ratio was **210 basis points (bps)** higher than the government target of **56.1%**.
**Fiscal Deficit Trajectory:** Fiscal deficit dropped significantly from **9.2% in FY21 to 4.4% in FY26**.
⚠️ **Target Trap:** Note that FY26 debt-to-GDP (58.2%) missed the government aim of 56.1% by 210 bps (2.1%).

blocks.text:
**Q:** How does the forward-looking ECL provisioning model improve bank balance sheets over the traditional incurred loss framework?

**Model Answer:** ECL mandates early provisioning based on historical trends and economic forecasts, preventing abrupt shock losses during credit downcycles.
